q: 1. A simply supported beam carries two equal concentrated loads W at distances L/3 from either support. The max BM is
explain: The reactions are W at each support. The BM between the two loads is constant and equal to Reaction * Distance = W * (L/3) = WL/3.

q: 2. The ratio of max deflection of a cantilever beam with an isolated load at free end and with a UDL over its entire length, is
explain: Deflection(Point) = WL³/3EI. Deflection(UDL) = WL³/8EI. The ratio is (1/3) / (1/8) = 8/3.

q: 3. If the length of a cantilever carrying an isolated load at its free end is doubled, the deflection... will increase by
explain: Deflection is proportional to L³. If length L is doubled, deflection increases by 2³ = 8 times.

q: 4. A beam extending beyond the support is called
explain: An overhanging beam has one or both of its end portions extending beyond the supports.

q: 5. A beam supported on more than two supports is called
explain: A continuous beam is a statically indeterminate structure that spans across more than two supports.

q: 6. The bending moment on a section is maximum where shear force is
explain: Since dM/dx = V, the maximum bending moment occurs where the shear force (V) is zero or changes sign.

q: 7. The shear force at the ends of a simply supported beam carrying a uniformly distributed load of w per unit length is
options: wl at one end and -wl at the other end
wl/2 at one end and -wl/2 at the other end
wl²/2 at one end and -wl²/2 at the other end
explain: For a symmetrical UDL, each support reaction is half the total load (W = wl). Therefore, the shear force starts at +wl/2 at one support and ends at -wl/2 at the other.

q: 8. In a beam where shear force changes sign, the bending moment will be
explain: A change in sign in the SFD indicates that the SF passes through zero, which identifies the location of the maximum bending moment.

q: 9. The number of reaction components possible at a fixed or built in end for a general loading
explain: A fixed support prevents all movement (vertical, horizontal, and rotation), providing three reactions: vertical force, horizontal force, and a bending moment.

q: 10. A simply supported beam is subjected to a pure moment. This will be resisted through
options: a moment reaction at hinged end
a moment reaction at hinge on rollers end
a couple formed by the reaction from the two supports
external support capable of resisting moment
explain: Since simple supports cannot provide moment reactions, the applied moment is balanced by a couple consisting of two equal and opposite vertical reactions at the supports.

q: 11. A simply supported beam is subjected to a udl of intensity W/m throughout the length of the span. The B.M. diagram will be a
explain: A UDL produces a 2nd-degree curve (parabola) for the bending moment, with the peak value at the center being wl²/8.

q: 12. A simply supported beam is subjected to a uniformly varying load with zero intensity at the two ends increasing to W/m at the centre. The maximum B.M. will be equal to
explain: For this specific triangular loading (apex at center), the maximum bending moment at the mid-span is calculated as wl²/12.

q: 13. The effect of arching a beam, is
options: to reduce the bending moment throughout
to increase the bending moment throughout
explain: Arching action converts some of the bending moments into axial thrust, thereby reducing the net bending moment that the material must resist.

q: 14. A member is balanced at its end by two inclined members carrying equal forces. For equilibrium the angle between the inclined bars must be
explain: For three equal forces to be in equilibrium at a joint, the angle between each pair of forces must be 120° (Lami's Theorem).

q: 15. The assumption in the theory of bending that the material is homogeneous and isotropic... implies that
options: the stresses are proportional to strains at all fibres
the strains are proportional to distances of the fibres from neutral axis
the beam bends into a circular arc
the neutral axis lies at the centre
explain: Homogeneity and isotropy imply consistent elastic properties throughout, which allows Hooke's Law (Stress ∝ Strain) to be applied uniformly.

q: 16. The moment of inertia of a rectangular section b x d about the base is
explain: Using Parallel Axis Theorem: I_base = I_cg + Ah² = (1/12 bd³) + (bd)(d/2)² = 1/3 bd³.

q: 17. When a beam is subjected to a bending moment, the strain in a layer is ............ the distance from the neutral axis.
explain: The fundamental assumption that 'plane sections remain plane' implies that longitudinal strain (ε) varies linearly with the distance (y) from the neutral axis.

q: 18. The bending equation is
explain: The Bernoulli-Euler bending equation relates the internal moment (M), moment of inertia (I), stress (σ), distance from neutral axis (y), modulus (E), and radius of curvature (R).

q: 19. A section of beam is said to be in pure bending, if it is subjected to
options: constant bending moment and constant shear force
constant shear force and zero bending moment
constant bending moment and zero shear force
explain: Pure bending (or simple bending) occurs in a region where the bending moment is constant, which mathematically implies the shear force (dM/dx) must be zero.

q: 20. The section modulus (Z) of a beam is given by
explain: Section modulus (Z) is defined as the ratio of the moment of inertia (I) to the distance of the extreme fiber from the neutral axis (y_max).

q: 21. The difference in placing the end of a beam simply over a support and the supporting end through a hinge on rollers is that the roller support
options: can offer reaction in the plane of rollers
will not allow the end to lift up due to deflection
will not offer reaction normal to the plane of rollers.
explain: A roller support provides a reaction only in the direction perpendicular to the plane of the rollers.

q: 22. Find the maximum SF induced in a cantilever beam subjected to a point load of 10 KN. Length of beam is 10 m. The load is located at a distance of 3 m from the free end
explain: For a single point load on a cantilever, the shear force between the fixed end and the load point equals the load itself, 10 kN.

q: 23. The maximum BM produced in a simply supported beam having span 4 m and subjected to a UDL of 10 kN/m
explain: M_max = wL²/8 = 10×4²/8 = 20 kN-m.

q: 24. Find the maximum SF induced in a S.S beam if the beam is subjected to a point load of 4 KN at the centre of beam and span of the beam is 4 m
explain: Each support reaction = W/2 = 4/2 = 2 kN, which is the maximum shear force.

q: 25. The relation between deflection (y) and bending moment (M) is
explain: The Euler-Bernoulli beam equation: M = -EI·d²y/dx² (sign convention dependent).

q: 26. The variation of the bending moment in the portion of the beam carrying linearly varying load is
explain: A linearly varying load (triangular) produces a shear force that's parabolic and a bending moment that's cubic in x.

q: 27. The maximum bending moment caused by a moving load on a fixed end beam occurs
explain: For a fixed-end beam, the largest bending moment from a moving load typically develops at the supports (fixed ends).

q: 28. If a cantilever beam carries a uniformly distributed load over its entire length, then the shape of the shear force diagram and bending moment diagram respectively are
explain: Under UDL, SF is linear (triangle) and BM is a second-degree (quadratic) parabola.

q: 29. The variation of the bending moment in the segment of a beam where no external load is present is
explain: With zero load, shear force is constant, so BM (its integral) varies linearly.

q: 30. The maximum bending moment caused by a moment M applied at a distance 'a' from one end on a simply supported beam is (where L=span, a>L/2)
explain: As per the answer key for this specific case (a > L/2).

q: 31. A beam is said to be of uniform strength if
options: bending moment is same throughout the beam
deflection is same throughout the beam
bending stress is same throughout the beam
explain: As per the answer key for this set (note: the classic textbook definition of 'uniform strength' is usually stated as constant bending stress throughout — worth double-checking against your source book if this seems inconsistent).

q: 32. The slope of an elastic curve at the point of contraflexure
explain: At a contraflexure point, only BM=0 is guaranteed; the slope can take any value there.

q: 33. In a beam, the neutral plane
options: passes through the c.g. of the area of c/s
explain: As per the answer key for this set (note: the standard textbook fact is that the neutral axis passes through the centroid of the cross-section — worth double-checking against your source book).

q: 34. The difference between BM values at any two sections will be equal to
options: the area of SF diagram between those two sections
the area of loading diagram between the two sections
the area of bending moment between the two sections
explain: ΔM between two sections equals the area under the shear force diagram between them (∫V dx).

q: 35. The bending moment in a cable carrying a system of loads will be
explain: A flexible cable carries load purely by axial tension along its curved shape — it develops no bending moment anywhere.

q: 36. The number of points of contraflexure in a simply supported beam carrying UDL, is
explain: A simply supported beam under UDL sags throughout its span, so BM never changes sign — zero contraflexure points.

q: 37. Moment of inertia of a rectangular beam b×d is
explain: Standard formula: I = bd³/12 about the centroidal axis parallel to b, with d as the depth.

q: 38. The shear force on a beam is proportional to
explain: Shear force at a section equals the algebraic sum of all transverse forces on one side of that section.

q: 39. In case of a simply supported beam subjected to UDL the maximum shear force occurs at a point
explain: For UDL on a simply supported beam, shear force is maximum at the supports and zero at mid-span.

q: 40. Shear force diagram for a cantilever carrying a UDL over its whole length is
explain: SF varies linearly from zero at the free end to wL at the fixed end — a triangle.

q: 41. In an I section almost all the shear force is taken by
explain: The web carries the vast majority (~90%+) of the transverse shear force in an I-section.

q: 42. If a constant section is subjected to a uniform/pure bending moment throughout, its length bends to
explain: Constant bending moment produces constant curvature — hence a circular arc.

q: 43. In a simply supported beam subjected to a point load at centre, the maximum bending moment occurs at
explain: For a central point load on a simply supported beam, max BM occurs directly under the load, at mid-span.

q: 44. A simply supported beam as shown carries 10 t of load, 2 m from support A and 3 m from support B. What will be the reaction at point B?
explain: RB = (Load × distance from A) / span = (10×2)/5 = 4 t.

q: 45. Bending moment diagram of a simply supported beam with a point load at the centre of the span is:
explain: BM rises linearly from zero at the supports to a peak under the central point load, forming a triangle.

q: 46. A beam is said to be loaded in pure bending when
options: Bending moment and shear force are changing linearly
explain: Pure bending is characterized by a constant bending moment (and correspondingly zero shear force) over the section of interest.

q: 47. If a cantilever beam of 8 m long has a uniformly distributed load of 2 KN/m throughout the length and a 10 KN point load at the center of beam, find the moment at center:
explain: Only the UDL beyond the center (4 m of it, total 8 kN, acting 2 m from center) contributes: 8×2 = 16 kN-m. The point load, applied exactly at the center, has zero moment arm about that same point.
